world.description: A Himalayan river valley at sunrise, built from scratch with no library assets.

path-pilgrim.name: Path from the footbridge to the pilgrim path

path-stair.name: Path from the footbridge to the monastery stair

pool-rim-boulders.name: Wet boulders round the plunge pool

intent.text: sunrise: low warm sun on the east slopes and gold roofs, cool blue shadows, light valley haze

himal-apricot.description: Apricot orchard tree: a short gnarled trunk twisting into 3-4 limbs under a rounded lumpy crown of leaf clusters, fresh green with apricot-orange fruit dots. Root at the origin, about 630 triangles.

himal-arch-bridge.description: Long multi-arched stone bridge along X: humped paved deck of individual setts, arch rings of voussoirs, piers with cutwaters, string courses, parapets with bevelled coping. Piers and abutments extend 'depth' m below the deck ends (bury them in the bed and banks). Lowest point y=0.

himal-boulder.description: Weathered boulder: a smooth lumpy mass with a flatter base bedded in the ground, darker underside, lichen on top. About 320 triangles at detail 2.

himal-channel.description: Irrigation channel along X: a soil bed with a flowing water ribbon, smooth rounded stone kerbs on both sides and loose cobbles, bowing along Z to follow a contour and dropping gently from -X to +X.

himal-chorten.description: White Tibetan chorten (stupa): mossy stone plinth, three bevelled whitewashed tiers with a red band, lathe-turned bell dome, harmika box, gilded 13-ring spire with parasol and finial; weathered plaster with grime and rain streaks.

himal-cliff.description: Rock wall behind the waterfall: a concave amphitheatre of bedded rock standing in front of the hanging-valley escarpment (the same height code and grid as himalaya-valley), from below the ground at the foot up to the lip of the hanging valley, its top rounding back into the plateau and its ends turning into the slope; jutting ledges at the top of each bed with undercuts and blocky joints, an overhanging brink, dark wet rock in the fall line, moss at the foot, fallen blocks; a plunge pool ringed with boulders bedded on the ground. Place at (cx, -20, cz).

himal-crag.description: Rocky crag for a monastery: flat level summit plateau (exactly `height` above the base), steep stratified limestone cliff band with ledges, a scree and soil apron easing into the ground; weathered rock with lichen and moss, exact trimesh collider. Optional stair spur: a rock rib on the +Z face (half width `spur`) rising in a straight line from the foot to the plateau edge at z = spurTop, for a stair to lie on.

himal-fence.description: Weathered timber field fence along X: tapered split posts every ~2 m with lashed, slightly sagging pole rails. Base y=0.

himal-field-wall.description: Dry-stone field wall along X: coursed rubble stones with a coping of upright stones, plus an optional buried footing of rougher, wider stones extending `footing` m below the wall base (so it can sit into a slope; the exposed part reads as a stone plinth).

footing.description: metres of buried footing below the normal wall base

himal-foam.description: Churning plunge-pool foam: flat ragged white foam ring and patches with holes showing water (mode pool), or white foam streaks running down an outflow stream (mode streak, descending along +X).

himal-goat.description: Small smooth Himalayan goat facing +X: 0.75 m shoulder, slim legs, backswept horns, beard, ears and tail; coat white/tan/black/piebald; headDown lowers the head to graze. Under 600 tris.

himal-gravel-bar.description: River gravel bar: a low lens-shaped shoal of rounded grey gravel with scattered pebbles and a few cobbles, damp at its edges

himal-house.description: Ladakhi / Tibetan village house: a rubble plinth set into the slope; battered whitewashed walls leaning in at a constant angle, in one volume or with the top storey set back over a roof terrace or stepped to one side (by seed); a rubble ground storey on some; a dark band under each parapet; a cornice of stacked timber (planks and a row of beam ends); a whitewashed parapet with rounded coping, rain spouts, brushwood and split firewood stacked on it; timber casements with black trapezoid surrounds and painted lintels with beam ends; a projecting timber bay (rabsal) on some; a rooftop room on some; an incense burner and prayer-flag poles on the roof corners with a string of flags across. Bevelled volumes.

found.description: foundation depth below the door ground (m): covers the fall of the slope under the footprint

wall.description: wall finish (auto: by seed and type)

himal-mani-wall.description: Mani wall: a long rubble wall carrying rows of carved slate prayer tablets, with whitewashed end caps, plus an optional buried footing of rougher, wider stones extending `footing` m below the wall base (so it can sit into a slope as a stone plinth).

footing.description: metres of buried footing below the normal wall base

himal-monastery.description: Tibetan hilltop gompa: a stone plinth, a battered whitewashed assembly hall with a stepped-back red upper hall, maroon penbey bands with gilded mirrors under timber cornices and parapets, rows of timber casements with black trapezoid surrounds, a red-pillared porch with a yak-hair curtain, a small red pavilion under two tiers of gilded roofs with upturned corners and a gilded pinnacle, victory banners on the corners, the dharma wheel and deer, white monks' wings round a paved courtyard, a courtyard wall with a gilded gate roof and prayer wheels. Front +Z; origin on the plateau centre, 0.5 m of foundation below y 0.

himal-outcrop.description: Sculpted rock outcrop: chiselled, noise-displaced rock mass with recessed bedding planes, flattened bedded base and angular scree at its feet. Smooth normals, under 1500 tris.

himal-prayer-flags.description: Prayer flag line along X between two weathered timber poles: a sagging cord carrying fluttering cloth flags in the five colours (blue, white, red, green, yellow). Base y=0.

himal-prayer-mill.description: Water-driven prayer wheel house: tapered dry-stone hut on a plinth, open doorway with oak frame and lintel, lathe-turned painted drum with brass bands on a vertical axle, slate gable roof with oak fascia and ridge, oak inlet/outlet flumes on trestles carrying water along X.

himal-range.description: Himalayan mountain range heightfield (pyramid peak, ridge or massif) with dark exposed rock below a ragged snowline, snow only on lying slopes and hollows, dark ribs and steep faces, cirque glaciers and distance haze.

himal-stack.description: Farm stack: variant 0 firewood pile of split bark logs in staggered rows with lighter end grain under a few flat capstones; variant 1 conical hay rick on a pole with straw texture. Base y=0.

himal-stair.description: Long monastery stone stair rising along +X: flights of worn stone treads on 1.2 m sloped slabs, stone landings carried on tapered piers, low parapet walls with coping along both sides; ramp colliders so it is walkable.

himal-suspension-bridge.description: Himalayan suspension footbridge spanning X: tapered stone plinths with timber portal towers on each bank (footings extend 'footing' m below the deck end), catenary main cables (tube), back stays to stone anchors, hanger ropes, rope handrails, a sagging deck of individual oak planks on stringers, and five-colour prayer flags hung along the cables. Lowest point y=0.

himal-temple.description: Himalayan village temple: stepped stone plinth, tapered whitewashed walls, red band under the eaves, timber beam ends, an overhanging roof with a gilded pyramidal pavilion and a brass finial, a carved door and window frames, and a covered prayer-wheel gallery round three sides

himal-terrace-field.description: One tile of the barley terraces at 0.5 m detail: the valley height function (same code and seed as himalaya-valley) stepped into contour terraces, crisp stone risers with a coping line, strips of ripe barley, green barley and fallow; parts outside the terrace zone sink under the valley ground. Place at (cx, -20, cz) with seed 7.

himal-terraces.description: Flight of curved barley terraces rising along +X: bowed field shelves following a contour, battered dry-stone retaining walls with stone coping, a buried skirt below the lowest wall.

himal-tree.description: Valley tree with a trunk and limbs carrying leaf-cluster cards (the renderer cuts the leaves out of each card) shingled over a dark inner mass, shaded light on the outside and dark within: variant 0 Lombardy poplar (a slim spindle on a straight trunk with short upswept limbs), 1 pollarded valley willow (a stout trunk, a knuckle of arching limbs, a domed crown with hanging curtains of leaves). Base y=0, trunk on the origin.

himal-tuft.description: Small grass tuft: 6-10 curved tapering blades (dark roots to pale tips) plus optional 0-4 flower heads; under 60 tris, base y=0.

himal-village-prop.description: Village props: 0 dry-stone yard wall along X, 1 leaning wooden ladder, 2 terracotta pot of marigolds, 3 washing line on two posts

himal-yak.description: Himalayan yak facing +X, one smooth-blended body: barrel, high shoulder hump, deep chest, low broad head; a shaggy skirt of long combed hair hanging from the flanks and belly, a tufted tail, tapered pale horns curving out, up and forward with dark tips, dark hooves. Base at y=0.

himalaya-river.description: Turquoise glacial river surface following the himalaya-valley channel; tiny corner anchors make its bounds match the terrain (place at the same position).

himalaya-valley.description: Himalayan river valley heightfield: river corridor, terraced barley fields, hanging-valley escarpment with waterfall notch and side stream, plus upper-slope gullies, strata ledges, scree/talus aprons, alluvial fans and slope/height/snow vertex colouring.

world.name: Himalayan Valley

source.prompt: dry-stone rubble wall of flat grey and ochre Himalayan fieldstones with thin dark mortar gaps
weathered grey-brown schist and granite rock face with fine layered strata, lichen flecks and cracks
high-altitude Himalayan meadow ground seen from above: short dry tawny grass tufts, bare earthy soil patches and small pebbles
rough hand-applied whitewashed lime plaster on a stone wall, uneven trowel marks, faint grey streaks and patches of wear
old weathered dark brown timber beam surface, deep grain, sun-dried cracks and worn edges, Tibetan house timber
worn mountain footpath of packed earth with rounded grey river cobbles and flat stepping stones pressed into it
